In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the international community has failed to create an effective global regime for water, and that it should instead concentrate its efforts on the development of effective MLG arrangements.
the failure of international regimes to develop hard law is not necessarily a sign of weakness.
the international community has failed in its efforts to develop a coherent global water regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the international regime is a useful tool in some circumstances, but not always.

the international community should focus on the creation of a global regime complex that is capable of dealing with the transnational nature of water issues, but that the national and sub-national levels of government should be the primary actors in the design and implementation of policy.
the international water community should focus more on developing MLG at the regional level than on developing international regimes at the global level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water governance needs to be approached from the bottom up rather than the top down.
water policy-making should be approached from the perspective of MLG and that the tools of MLG are more important to the success of water policy-making than the existence of hard law.
water is best dealt with at a sub-national or regional level and that international agreements can be most effective in providing a framework for such regional efforts.
